proposals.citation: Chen B, Zhang C, Yuan Y, Wang Z, Cui T, Dong G, Pan H, Zhang Z, Li W. Novel PNPLA8 variants associated with primary ovarian insufficiency, tremors, cerebellar ataxia and limb weakness: a case report and literature review. J Neurol 272: 78, 2024. [PubMed: 39680195]
proposals.label: Chen et al. (2024)
proposals.rationale: Chen et al. (2024) report two PNPLA8 variants that are not in the variant table: c.1777T>G (p.Tyr593Asp) and c.1515_1516delTT (p.Tyr506Serfs*27). They occurred in a Chinese woman whose illness began in late childhood and was milder than in earlier cases, with primary ovarian insufficiency (amenorrhea, infantile uterus), head and limb tremors, and cerebellar ataxia; none of these features is in the entry. The paper also reviews 25 patients from 21 families and proposes that age of onset correlates with phenotype and prognosis.

paragraphs.text: Chen et al. (2024) reported a 27-year-old Chinese woman whose gait became abnormal at age 11 years. At age 17 she still had amenorrhea and an infantile uterus, and at age 21 she developed head and limb tremors. Brain MRI suggested mild cerebellar atrophy. On a biceps muscle biopsy, light microscopy showed mild myopathic changes and electron microscopy showed mitochondrial inclusions.

In a 27-year-old Chinese woman with cerebellar ataxia, tremors, and primary ovarian insufficiency, Chen et al. (2024) used whole-exome sequencing to identify compound heterozygous mutations in the PNPLA8 gene. One was a missense mutation, c.1777T-G, resulting in a tyr593-to-asp (Y593D) substitution. The other was a frameshift mutation, c.1515_1516delTT, predicted to cause p.Tyr506SerfsTer27. She had inherited the mutations from her parents.

Chen et al. (2024) reviewed 25 patients from 21 families with PNPLA8 variants and concluded that age of onset is a very important factor in the clinical phenotype and prognosis. They observed that adult females with PNPLA8 variants may present with primary ovarian dysfunction, and they suggested that mitochondrial inclusion bodies may be a pathologic hallmark of the disorder.

quotes: A 27-year-old Chinese woman presented with abnormal gait at age 11, remained amenorrhoeic with an infantile uterus at age 17, and presented with head and limb tremors at age 21.
The results of brain magnetic resonance imaging suggested mild cerebellar atrophy.
Her muscle biopsy showed mild myopathic changes on light microscopy and mitochondrial inclusions on electron microscopy.

The patient's genetic screening revealed compound heterozygous variants c.1777T > G (p.Tyr593Asp) and c.1515-1516delTT (p.Tyr506Serfs*27) of PNPLA8 inherited from her parents.

proposals.citation: Moon SH, Dilthey BG, Guan S, Sims HF, Pittman SK, Keith AL, Jenkins CM, Weihl CC, Gross RW. Genetic deletion of skeletal muscle iPLA2γ results in mitochondrial dysfunction, muscle atrophy and alterations in whole-body energy metabolism. iScience 26: 106895, 2023. [PubMed: 37275531]
proposals.label: Moon et al. (2023)
proposals.rationale: This is the first skeletal muscle-specific Pnpla8 (iPLA2-gamma) knockout mouse; the entry's animal-model data cover only global null mice. The new model establishes a muscle-restricted myopathy phenotype (weakness, atrophy, raised blood lactate, damaged mitochondria) and adds mechanistic detail: defective respiration with reduced complex I/II/IV activity, lower mitochondrial membrane potential, decreased mtDNA copy number, loss of tetra-18:2 cardiolipin, impaired Akt/mTOR protein synthesis, and systemic metabolic effects.

paragraphs.text: Moon et al. (2023) generated a skeletal muscle-specific iPLA2-gamma (Pnpla8) knockout mouse (SKMiPLA2gammaKO) by crossing mice carrying loxP sites flanking exon 5, which encodes the enzyme active site, with transgenic mice expressing Cre recombinase from the human alpha-actin promoter. Western blot analysis of mitochondria from white adipose tissue, liver, and skeletal muscle confirmed that ablation of iPLA2-gamma was restricted to skeletal muscle. The knockout mice had pronounced muscle weakness, muscle atrophy, and increased blood lactate resulting from mitochondrial defects that impaired the metabolic processing of pyruvate and caused bioenergetic inefficiency; the authors concluded that this established a multicomponent myopathy affecting skeletal muscle bioenergetics, mechanical function, and whole-body energy metabolism. Tibialis anterior and quadriceps muscle mass was decreased by 30% in males, with a greater loss of tibialis anterior mass in females. Transmission electron microscopy of tibialis anterior muscle from 7-month-old knockout mice showed a prevalence of mitochondria with severe ultrastructural damage, including irregular cristae and electron-dense inclusions, along with disruption of the normal striated muscle structure. Histology showed internalization of nuclei, smaller myocyte diameter, and irregularly sized myofibers with increased numbers of markedly smaller myofibers; myogenin expression was markedly increased while MyoD was unchanged, indicating active regenerative myogenesis, and the fast-twitch tibialis anterior shifted further toward a type II fiber phenotype.

Moon et al. (2023) found that mitochondrial DNA copy number, assessed as ND1 relative to nuclear HK2, was significantly decreased in SKMiPLA2gammaKO tibialis anterior muscle, and that protein levels of the mitochondrial fusion/fission proteins DRP1, OPA1, and MFN1 were dramatically diminished despite only modest decreases in their mRNA, whereas the mitochondrial markers VDAC, ANT, and citrate synthase and the ratio of recoverable mitochondrial protein to muscle mass were unchanged. Protein synthesis through the Akt/mTOR pathway involving S6 ribosomal protein was significantly impaired, with marked decreases in phosphorylation despite compensatory upregulation of Akt and S6 protein mass and prominent cleavage of mTOR, while autophagic flux (LC3B-I/II and p62) was unchanged; the authors concluded that reduced net protein synthesis in the setting of bioenergetic inefficiency likely underlay the muscle atrophy.

Moon et al. (2023) found in 7- to 8-month-old mice that SKMiPLA2gammaKO animals had weaker grip force and fatigued more rapidly during treadmill exercise, irrespective of diet or sex, and that serum lactate after exercise rose more in knockout than wild-type mice despite shorter exercise duration. During high-intensity exercise at 18 m/min for 4 min, 3 of 6 knockout female mice were completely exhausted within 1 to 2.5 min, with marked blood lactate accumulation and a corresponding decline in blood glucose compared with wild-type counterparts. By ex vivo isometric force measurement of extensor digitorum longus muscle from 4 wild-type and 4 knockout mice, muscle weight, total body weight, and physiological cross-sectional area were lower in knockouts, but specific tetanic peak tension after normalization to cross-sectional area did not differ between genotypes, which the authors noted limited their ability to exclude neurological or behavioral contributions to the weakness.

Moon et al. (2023) used high-resolution respirometry of saponin-permeabilized tibialis anterior muscle and found that mitochondria from normal-chow-fed male SKMiPLA2gammaKO mice consumed 50% less oxygen than wild-type controls with glutamate/pyruvate/malate as substrate, with an even larger difference in females. Protein levels of complex IV and cytochrome c were dramatically reduced, and although complex I and II protein levels were unchanged, their catalytic activities were decreased by about 50% and 25%, respectively. Mitochondrial membrane potential measured with a tetraphenylphosphonium electrode in mitochondria from 5 wild-type and 5 knockout mice was significantly lower in knockouts with either complex I or complex II substrates, and hydrogen peroxide production from forward and reverse electron transfer was greatly attenuated. By multidimensional mass spectrometry-based shotgun lipidomics, knockout tibialis anterior muscle had significantly lower levels of tetra-18:2 cardiolipin, the most abundant mature cardiolipin species in skeletal muscle, and decreased 22:6-containing cardiolipin species; the authors suggested that loss of tetra-18:2 cardiolipin contributes to inefficient respiration by disrupting the stability and association of electron transport chain proteins.

Moon et al. (2023) reported that SKMiPLA2gammaKO mice were resistant to high-fat diet-induced weight gain, gaining on average about 8 g versus about 16 g in wild-type mice after 3 months of high-fat feeding, and showed improved glucose clearance with a lower peak glucose (about 240 versus about 320 mg/dL) and decreased area under the curve during glucose challenge, without significant differences in insulin tolerance or serum insulin. High-fat-fed knockout mice had dramatically less hepatic lipid droplet content, lower hepatic triacylglycerol and diacylglycerol species, no increase in liver-to-body weight ratio, diminished high-fat diet-induced hepatic fibrosis, and higher hepatic glycogen than wild-type controls, while high-fat diet-induced increases in white adipose tissue mass were significantly more prominent in the knockout.

Moon et al. (2023) concluded that iPLA2-gamma mediates skeletal muscle bioenergetic function through preservation of mitochondrial structural and functional integrity, maintenance of an appropriate membrane environment for assembly of protein complexes, and concerted signaling of skeletal muscle with the liver, and that the compromised bioenergetic and physiologic phenotype of the knockout mouse was due to multifactorial mitochondrial dysfunction for which no single precipitating cause could be identified.

evidence.statement: Moon et al. (2023) generated a skeletal muscle-specific iPLA2gamma (PNPLA8) knockout mouse (SKMiPLA2gammaKO) by crossing mice carrying loxP sites flanking exon 5 of the iPLA2gamma gene, which encodes the enzyme active site, with transgenic mice expressing Cre recombinase driven by the human alpha-actin promoter; western blot analysis of mitochondria from white adipose tissue, liver and skeletal muscle confirmed that ablation of iPLA2gamma was restricted to skeletal muscle.
quotes: To generate the skeletal muscle-specific iPLA2γ KO mouse, exon 5 (encoding the iPLA2γ active site) was flanked by loxP sites as described previously and ablated by crossing with a transgenic mouse expressing Cre-recombinase driven by the human alpha-actin promoter (The Jackson Laboratory, Cat. # 006149).

Importantly, the expression levels of the iPLA2γ isoforms in liver and white adipose tissue from the SKMiPLA2γKO mouse were unchanged in comparison to those present in WT mice (Figure 1A). In contrast, mitochondrial iPLA2γ protein expression levels in skeletal muscle tissues were nearly completely ablated in SKMiPLA2γKO mice.

evidence.statement: Moon et al. (2023) reported that genetic ablation of skeletal muscle iPLA2gamma in the mouse produced pronounced muscle weakness, muscle atrophy, and increased blood lactate resulting from defects in mitochondrial function that impaired metabolic processing of pyruvate and caused bioenergetic inefficiency; the authors concluded that these findings established a multicomponent myopathy with pathophysiologic effects on skeletal muscle bioenergetics, mechanical function, and whole-body energy metabolism.
quotes: Genetic ablation of skeletal muscle iPLA2γ resulted in pronounced muscle weakness, muscle atrophy, and increased blood lactate resulting from defects in mitochondrial function impairing metabolic processing of pyruvate and resultant bioenergetic inefficiency.

These critical roles of skeletal muscle iPLA2γ are underscored by the clear presence of a multicomponent myopathy that has pathophysiologic effects on skeletal muscle bioenergetics, mechanical function, and whole-body energy metabolism.

evidence.statement: Moon et al. (2023) found that tibialis anterior and quadriceps muscle mass was decreased by 30% in male SKMiPLA2gammaKO mice, with a greater loss of tibialis anterior mass in females; transmission electron microscopy of tibialis anterior muscle from 7-month-old knockout mice showed a prevalence of mitochondria with severe ultrastructural damage including irregular cristae and electron dense inclusions, accompanied by disruption of normal striated muscle structure.
quotes: A prominent physical difference of the SKMiPLA2γKO mouse in comparison to WT controls was the decrease in the size/weight of the tibialis anterior (TA) and quadriceps (Quad) muscle groups that were decreased by 30% in male mice (Figure 1B). Examination of gender differences demonstrated a greater loss of TA mass in females in comparison to males by deletion of iPLA2γ.

TEM image analysis of the TA muscle from WT and KO mice demonstrated a prevalence of mitochondria with severe ultrastructural damage, including irregular cristae and electron dense inclusions present in the KO mouse accompanied by the disruption of normal striated muscle structure (Figures 1C and S1).

evidence.statement: Moon et al. (2023) showed that mitochondrial DNA copy number, assessed as ND1 relative to nuclear HK2 by qPCR, was significantly decreased in SKMiPLA2gammaKO tibialis anterior muscle, and that protein levels of the mitochondrial fusion/fission proteins DRP1, OPA1 and MFN1 were dramatically diminished despite only modest decreases in their mRNA levels, whereas the ratio of recoverable mitochondrial protein to muscle mass and the mitochondrial markers VDAC, ANT and citrate synthase were unchanged.
quotes: In contrast, mtDNA copy number in SKMiPLA2γKO TA muscle was significantly decreased indicating alterations in mitochondrial content due to disrupted -mtDNA maintenance processes (Figure 1E). Furthermore, despite only modest decreases in mRNA levels of DRP1, OPA1, and MFN1 relative to WT controls, the expression levels of these proteins were dramatically diminished in SKMiPLA2γKO TA muscle, which likely contributed to the observed decrease in mtDNA copy number and the altered morphology of the mitochondria (Figures 1F and S2).

This result was supported by western blot analyses showing no significant differences in normalized expression levels of abundant mitochondrial marker proteins including VDAC, ANT, and citrate synthase (CS) from WT and iPLA2γ KO TA muscle tissue (Figure 1F).

evidence.statement: Moon et al. (2023) reported that protein synthesis through the Akt/mTOR muscle growth pathway involving S6 ribosomal protein was significantly impaired in SKMiPLA2gammaKO muscle, with marked decreases in phosphorylation of these proteins despite compensatory upregulation of Akt and S6 protein mass and prominent cleavage of mTOR, while autophagic flux monitored by LC3B-I/II and p62 was unchanged; they concluded that reduced net protein synthesis in the setting of bioenergetic inefficiency likely underlay the muscle atrophy.
quotes: The results indicated that protein synthesis via the Akt/mTOR muscle growth pathway involving S6 ribosomal protein activation was significantly impaired due to dramatic decreases in phosphorylation (indicating activation) of these proteins despite compensatory upregulation of Akt and S6 protein mass (Figure 1G).

Autophagocytic flux monitored by LC3B-I/II and p62 (p62/SQSTM1) protein expression levels was not significantly changed in SKMiPLA2γKO mouse TA muscle when compared with WT controls (Figure 1G). Thus, reduction of the net rate of protein synthesis in the presence of bioenergetic inefficiency likely underlies the skeletal muscle atrophy present in the SKMiPLA2γKO mouse.

evidence.statement: Moon et al. (2023) found in grip and treadmill tests of 7- to 8-month-old mice that SKMiPLA2gammaKO mice had weaker grip force and fatigued more rapidly during treadmill exercise, irrespective of diet type or sex, and that serum lactate after treadmill exercise rose more in knockout than wild-type mice despite a shorter average exercise duration.
quotes: Both grip tests and treadmill exercise tests revealed that the iPLA2γ KO mouse had a weaker grip force and was more rapidly fatigued during treadmill exercise. These results indicate that deletion of skeletal muscle iPLA2γ resulted in compromised skeletal muscle mechanical function.
Conversely, serum lactate levels present in the SKMiPLA2γKO mouse after exercise on the treadmill increased more than WT despite a shorter average exercise duration time (Figure 2E).

evidence.statement: Moon et al. (2023) reported that in high-intensity treadmill exercise at 18 m/min for 4 min, 3 of 6 SKMiPLA2gammaKO female mice were completely exhausted within 1 to 2.5 min, and blood lactate accumulation markedly increased with a corresponding decline in blood glucose in the knockout compared with wild-type counterparts.
quotes: Note that 3 out of 6 KO mice were completely exhausted within 1–2.5 min and their glucose and lactate levels were measured immediately upon reaching exhaustion.

Consistent with the respiration results with isolated mitochondria, lactate accumulation in the blood of the SKMiPLA2γKO mouse markedly increased with a corresponding decline in blood glucose following intense exercise in comparisons with their WT counterparts (Figures 3G and 3H).

evidence.statement: Moon et al. (2023) found that histology of tibialis anterior muscle from SKMiPLA2gammaKO mice showed internalization of nuclei and smaller myocyte diameter, with quadriceps showing irregularly sized myocytes and increased numbers of markedly smaller myofibers; myogenin expression was markedly increased while MyoD was unchanged, indicating more active regenerative myogenesis, and fast-twitch tibialis anterior muscle was further shifted toward a fast-twitch type II fiber phenotype.
quotes: TA muscle cross sections from the SKMiPLA2γKO mouse displayed internalization of nuclei and a smaller apparent myocyte diameter while those from WT had a relatively larger diameter and multiple peripheral nuclei (Figure 2H).

Although expression levels of the myogenic regulatory factor MyoD were essentially unchanged in the SKMiPLA2γKO in comparison to WT controls, markedly increased expression of Myogenin due to iPLA2γ loss of function in skeletal muscle is indicative of more active regenerative myogenesis in SKMiPLA2γKO vs. WT mice (Figure 2I).

Interestingly, fast-twitch TA muscle from the SKMiPLA2γKO mouse was further shifted toward a fast-twitch type II muscle fiber phenotype as determined by western blot analysis for fast- and slow-skeletal muscle myosin (Figure 2G).

evidence.statement: Moon et al. (2023) showed by ex vivo isometric force measurement of extensor digitorum longus muscle from 4 wild-type and 4 SKMiPLA2gammaKO mice that EDL muscle weight and total body weight were lower in knockouts, giving a smaller physiological cross-sectional area, but that specific tetanic peak tension after normalization to cross-sectional area did not differ between genotypes; the authors noted this limited the ability to exclude neurological or behavioral contributions to the weakness.
quotes: EDL muscle weight as well as the total body weight of the SKMiPLA2γKO mouse were lower than WT controls resulting in a smaller physiological cross-sectional area (PCSA). Muscle force measurements indicated that specific tetanic peak tensions after normalization to PCSA were not different between WT and SKMiPLA2γKO mice (Figure 2F).

However, since no difference in specific force was observed, we cannot exclude the possibility of neurological and/or behavioral defects in the SKMiPLA2γKO mouse contributing to muscle weakness and atrophy.

evidence.statement: Moon et al. (2023) used high-resolution respirometry of saponin-permeabilized tibialis anterior muscle and found that mitochondria from normal-chow-fed male SKMiPLA2gammaKO mice consumed 50% less oxygen than wild-type controls with glutamate/pyruvate/malate as substrate, with an even larger difference in females; protein levels of complex IV and cytochrome c were dramatically reduced, and although complex I and II protein levels were unchanged, their catalytic activities were decreased by about 50% and 25%, respectively.
quotes: Consistent with the above results, TA mitochondria isolated from SKMiPLA2γKO male mice on an NC-diet consumed 50% less oxygen than WT controls under same conditions (Figure 3A).

Interestingly, the protein expression levels of complex IV and cytochrome c in SKMiPLA2γKO skeletal muscle were dramatically reduced in comparison to WT littermates (Figure 3B). Moreover, although the expression levels of complexes I and II were not detectably altered in KO TA muscle, the individually measured activities of complexes I and II were decreased by ∼ 50% and ∼ 25%, respectively, when compared with WT controls (Figures 3C and 3D).

evidence.statement: Moon et al. (2023) measured mitochondrial membrane potential with a tetraphenylphosphonium electrode in mitochondria isolated from tibialis anterior muscle of 5 wild-type and 5 knockout mice and found it significantly lower in SKMiPLA2gammaKO mice with either complex I (glutamate/pyruvate/malate) or complex II (succinate) substrates, and that hydrogen peroxide production from forward and reverse electron transfer was greatly attenuated in the knockout.
quotes: The mitochondrial membrane potential in SKMiPLA2γKO mouse TA muscle with complex I or complex II substrates (i.e., glutamate/pyruvate/malate or succinate, respectively) was significantly lower than that of WT littermates (Figure 3E).

Consistent with the lower membrane potential of SKMiPLA2γKO mitochondria, hydrogen peroxide production indicative of ROS generated from forward (i.e., observed with glutamate/pyruvate/malate with rotenone) and reverse (i.e., observed with succinate) electron transfer was greatly attenuated in SKMiPLA2γKO mice in comparison with WT controls (Figure 3F).

evidence.statement: Moon et al. (2023) used multidimensional mass spectrometry-based shotgun lipidomics and found that SKMiPLA2gammaKO tibialis anterior muscle had significantly lower levels of tetra-18:2 cardiolipin, the most abundant mature cardiolipin species in skeletal muscle, and decreased 22:6-containing cardiolipin species during normal-chow feeding; the authors suggested that loss of tetra-18:2 cardiolipin contributes to inefficient respiration by disrupting the stability and association of electron transport chain proteins.
quotes: The results indicated that SKMiPLA2γKO TA muscle possessed significantly lower levels of tetra 18:2 CL, the most abundant mature form of CL molecular species in skeletal muscle, as well as decreased 22:6-containing CL molecular species during NC feeding.

These data suggest that loss of tetra-18:2 CL contributes to inefficient respiration through disruption of the stability and/or the association of ETC proteins likely resulting from alterations in mitochondrial membrane surface charge and molecular dynamics.

evidence.statement: Moon et al. (2023) found that SKMiPLA2gammaKO mice were resistant to high-fat diet-induced weight gain, gaining on average about 8 g versus about 16 g in wild-type mice after 3 months of high-fat feeding, and showed improved glucose clearance with a lower peak glucose (about 240 versus about 320 mg/dL) and decreased area under the curve during glucose challenge, without significant differences in insulin tolerance or serum insulin levels.
quotes: Specifically, the net body mass increase of the SKMiPLA2γKO mouse following consumption of an HF diet was on average ∼ 8g while WT mice gained ∼ 16g after 3-month of HF feeding (Figures 5A and 5B).

In contrast, SKMiPLA2γKO mice displayed an improved response to glucose challenge resulting in a peak concentration of ∼ 240 mg glucose/dl and the decreased area under the curve during glucose challenge (Figure 5H).

Although the SKMiPLA2γKO mice exhibited a lower basal blood glucose level after HF feeding than wild-type controls, no significant differences in insulin tolerance and serum insulin levels in WT vs. KO were observed (Figures 5J and 5K).

evidence.statement: Moon et al. (2023) reported that high-fat-fed SKMiPLA2gammaKO mice had dramatically less hepatic lipid droplet content, significantly lower hepatic triacylglycerol and diacylglycerol molecular species, no increase in liver-to-body weight ratio, diminished high-fat diet-induced fibrosis, and higher hepatic glycogen content than wild-type controls, while high-fat diet-induced increases in white adipose tissue mass were significantly more prominent in the knockout.
quotes: First, utilizing H & E staining and imaging, we found that the content of lipid droplets present in the HF-fed SKMiPLA2γKO liver was dramatically less than HF-fed WT controls (Figure 6A).
Higher amounts of glycogen were present in iPLA2γ KO liver in comparison to WT liver controls (Figure 7A).
Interestingly, HF diet-induced increases in white adipose tissue mass were significantly more prominent in SKMiPLA2γKO mice than WT controls (Figure 5D).

evidence.statement: Moon et al. (2023) concluded that iPLA2gamma mediates skeletal muscle bioenergetic function through preservation of mitochondrial structural and functional integrity, maintenance of an appropriate membrane environment for assembly of protein complexes, and concerted signaling of skeletal muscle with the liver, and that the compromised bioenergetic and physiologic phenotype of the skeletal muscle iPLA2gamma knockout mouse was due to multifactorial mitochondrial dysfunction for which no single precipitating cause could be identified.
quotes: Collectively, the present study demonstrates that iPLA2γ mediates skeletal muscle bioenergetic function through multiple mechanisms including: 1) the preservation of mitochondrial structural and functional integrity; 2) the appropriate membrane environment (e.g., surface charge, assembly of protein complexes, mitochondrial membrane morphology for optimal mitochondria function; and 3) concerted signaling of skeletal muscle with the liver for inter-organ impedance matching to facilitate metabolic flexibility in organismal bioenergetics.

The observed mitochondrial dysfunction is multifactorial in nature and it is not possible to identify a single precipitating cause. Nevertheless, the results clearly identify that the compromised bioenergetic and physiologic phenotype of the skeletal muscle iPLA2γ KO mouse is due to mitochondrial dysfunction.

evidence.statement: Moon et al. (2023), reviewing prior work motivating their study, noted that the relevance of iPLA2gamma-mediated pathologies in humans was underscored by the discovery through exome sequencing of a severely ill patient null for both iPLA2gamma alleles due to a premature stop codon in both alleles, who demonstrated marked mitochondrial morphologic alterations, muscle weakness, and lactic acidosis, and that a subsequent study reported two more unrelated patients with loss-of-function variants in PNPLA8 and similar pathologic alterations.
quotes: Furthermore, the relevance of iPLA2γ-mediated pathologies in humans was underscored by the discovery of a severely ill patient null for both iPLA2γ alleles that was identified through exome sequencing identifying a premature stop codon for iPLA2γ in both alleles. This patient demonstrated marked mitochondrial morphologic alterations, muscle weakness, and lactic acidosis.
A subsequent study reported two more unrelated patients with loss-of-function variants in PNPLA8 encoding iPLA2γ and similar pathologic alterations.
